reason: سْمِ is governed by the prefixed بِ in the formula بِسْمِ.
ٱللَّهِ is the genitive muḍāf ilayhi of سْمِ.
ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ follows ٱللَّهِ in genitive definiteness as an adjectival divine epithet.
ٱلرَّحِيمِ follows ٱللَّهِ in the same genitive adjectival series.
أَلَمْ contains لَمْ, which governs تَرَ in the jussive.
تَرَ governs the indirect question beginning with كَيْفَ.
كَيْفَ asks the manner of فَعَلَ inside the embedded question.
رَبُّكَ is nominative after فَعَلَ and supplies its explicit subject.
The suffix كَ in رَبُّكَ is the genitive possessor of رَبّ.
أَصْحَٰبِ is governed by بِ as the complement of فَعَلَ.
ٱلْفِيلِ is the genitive complement in the iḍāfa أَصْحَٰبِ ٱلْفِيلِ.
أَلَمْ contains لَمْ, which governs يَجْعَلْ in the jussive.
كَيْدَهُمْ is the accusative object of يَجْعَلْ.
The suffix هُمْ in كَيْدَهُمْ is the genitive possessor of كَيْد.
تَضْلِيلٍ is governed by فِى as the result-state complement of يَجْعَلْ.
The suffix هُمْ in عَلَيْهِمْ is governed by عَلَى as the target complement of أَرْسَلَ.
طَيْرًا is the accusative direct object of أَرْسَلَ.
أَبَابِيلَ can describe the accusative indefinite طَيْرًا as birds in flocks.
أَبَابِيلَ can also be read as a ḥāl describing طَيْرًا as they were sent.
The suffix هِمْ in تَرْمِيهِم is the object pronoun of تَرْمِي.
حِجَارَةٍ is governed by the prefixed بِ in بِحِجَارَةٍ as the instrument complement of تَرْمِي.
سِجِّيلٍ is governed by مِن to specify the kind or source of حِجَارَةٍ.
The suffix هُمْ in جَعَلَهُمْ is the direct object of جَعَلَ.
عَصْفٍ is governed by كَ as the comparison complement of جَعَلَ.
مَّأْكُولٍ agrees with and modifies عَصْفٍ.
